title: Network
description: The router's DNS queries (dnsmasq log-queries) and firewall drops, from its syslog in VictoriaLogs.

panels.title: Queries
panels.description: DNS queries the router received from clients.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns event.action:=dns-query | count() as queries

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: Distinct clients asking (client.ip).

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns event.action:=dns-query | count_uniq(client.ip) as clients

panels.title: Domains
panels.description: Distinct names asked for.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns event.action:=dns-query | count_uniq(dns.question.name) as domains

panels.title: NXDOMAIN
panels.description: Answers saying the name doesn't exist (typos, ad blocking upstream, or malware trying generated names).

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns dns.type:=answer dns.response_code:=NXDOMAIN | count() as answers

panels.title: Not via Pi-hole
panels.description: Queries the router forwarded somewhere other than Pi-hole (192.168.111.100): its fallback when Pi-hole doesn't answer, so unfiltered.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns event.action:=dns-forwarded -destination.ip:=192.168.111.100 | count() as queries

panels.title: Failed answers
panels.description: SERVFAIL and REFUSED answers: upstream trouble.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns dns.type:=answer dns.response_code:in(SERVFAIL, REFUSED) | count() as answers

panels.title: Queries by client
panels.description: Queries per client address.

targets.expr: {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns event.action:=dns-query | stats by (client.ip) count() as queries

panels.title: Forwarded upstream
panels.description: Where the router sent queries it couldn't answer itself: Pi-hole, or its fallback.

targets.expr: {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns event.action:=dns-forwarded | stats by (destination.ip) count() as queries

panels.title: Other DNS servers
panels.description: Where the router sent queries instead of Pi-hole (192.168.111.100): its fallback upstream when Pi-hole doesn't answer, so these queries weren't filtered. Pi-hole being down or slow shows here. A device using its own DNS server directly (not the router) isn't in the router's DNS log.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns event.action:=dns-forwarded -destination.ip:=192.168.111.100 | stats by (destination.ip) count() as queries, count_uniq(client.ip) as clients, count_uniq(dns.question.name) as domains, max(_time) as _time | sort by (queries desc)

panels.title: Queries not via Pi-hole
panels.description: Each name the router looked up somewhere other than Pi-hole, who asked (the client from log-queries=extra) and which DNS server answered it.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns event.action:=dns-forwarded -destination.ip:=192.168.111.100 | stats by (destination.ip, dns.question.name, client.ip) count() as queries, max(_time) as _time | sort by (_time desc) | limit 200

panels.title: Top domains
panels.description: The most asked-for names, with how many clients asked.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns event.action:=dns-query | stats by (dns.question.name) count() as queries, count_uniq(client.ip) as clients, max(_time) as _time | sort by (queries desc) | limit 100

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: Each client: queries, distinct names, record types. Click one to investigate it.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns event.action:=dns-query | stats by (client.ip) count() as queries, count_uniq(dns.question.name) as domains, max(_time) as _time | sort by (queries desc) | limit 50

panels.title: Names that don't exist
panels.description: NXDOMAIN answers by name. Many random-looking names from one client can be malware (DGA).

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" network.protocol:=dns dns.type:=answer dns.response_code:=NXDOMAIN | stats by (dns.question.name) count() as answers, max(_time) as _time | sort by (answers desc) | limit 100

panels.title: Dropped
panels.description: Packets the router's firewall dropped (Firewall > Logged packets: Dropped).

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop | count() as packets

panels.title: From the internet
panels.description: Drops from public addresses: scans and noise, expected.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop -(source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") or source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") or source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) | count() as packets

panels.title: From the LAN
panels.description: Drops from private addresses: a device trying something the firewall forbids.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop (source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") or source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") or source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) | count() as packets

panels.title: Sources
panels.description: Distinct source addresses dropped.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop | count_uniq(source.ip) as sources

panels.title: Ports
panels.description: Distinct destination ports dropped.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop | count_uniq(destination.port) as ports

panels.title: Accepted (logged)
panels.description: Connections the router let through (nat-start's LOG_ACCEPT chain), one line each: the Accepted connections row below has them by way out.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept | count() as packets

panels.title: Drops
panels.description: Dropped packets, from the internet and from the LAN.

targets.expr: {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop -(source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") or source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") or source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) | stats count() as packets

{event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop (source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") or source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") or source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) | stats count() as packets

panels.title: Drops by port
panels.description: Dropped packets per destination port.

targets.expr: {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop | stats by (destination.port) count() as packets

panels.title: Where they come from
panels.description: Dropped packets from the internet by where the source address is: one point per place, bigger for more packets. Approximate below country level. Map tiles from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors; Grafana's default, CARTO, needs an API key). Where an address is: IP geolocation by DB-IP (https://db-ip.com), CC BY 4.0.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop -(source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") or source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") or source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) source.geo.location.lat:* | stats by (source.geo.location.lat, source.geo.location.lon, source.geo.country_name, source.geo.city_name) count() as packets, count_uniq(source.ip) as sources

panels.title: Countries
panels.description: Dropped packets from the internet by the source address's country. Where an address is: IP geolocation by DB-IP (https://db-ip.com), CC BY 4.0.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop -(source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") or source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") or source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) | stats by (source.geo.country_iso_code, source.geo.country_name) count() as packets, count_uniq(source.ip) as sources | sort by (packets desc) | limit 50

panels.title: Networks
panels.description: Dropped packets from the internet by the network (autonomous system) the source address belongs to: hosting providers are usually scanners. Where an address is: IP geolocation by DB-IP (https://db-ip.com), CC BY 4.0.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop -(source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") or source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") or source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) | stats by (source.as.number, source.as.organization.name) count() as packets, count_uniq(source.ip) as sources | sort by (packets desc) | limit 50

panels.title: Internet sources
panels.description: Public addresses dropped most, with how many ports they tried, their country and network. Where an address is: IP geolocation by DB-IP (https://db-ip.com), CC BY 4.0.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop -(source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") or source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") or source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) | stats by (source.ip, source.geo.country_iso_code, source.as.organization.name) count() as packets, count_uniq(destination.port) as ports, max(_time) as _time | sort by (packets desc) | limit 50

panels.title: Ports
panels.description: Destination ports dropped most, by protocol.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop | stats by (network.transport, destination.port) count() as packets, count_uniq(source.ip) as sources, max(_time) as _time | sort by (packets desc) | limit 50

panels.title: LAN drops
panels.description: Drops from private addresses: which device, to where.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop (source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") or source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") or source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) | stats by (source.ip, destination.ip, network.transport, destination.port) count() as packets, max(_time) as _time | sort by (packets desc) | limit 50

panels.title: Dropped packets
panels.description: The latest drops, newest first.

targets.expr: {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop

panels.title: Through the VPN
panels.description: Connections out through the WireGuard tunnel (wgc1).

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept observer.egress.interface.name:=wgc1 | count() as connections

panels.title: Straight out
panels.description: Devices' connections straight out the WAN (ppp0), not through the VPN: VPN Director's exceptions. The router's own traffic, from its WAN address, isn't counted.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept observer.egress.interface.name:=ppp0 (source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") or source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") or source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) | count() as connections

panels.title: Between networks
panels.description: Connections the router passed from one of its networks to another (out a br bridge).

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept observer.egress.interface.name:~"^br" | count() as connections

panels.title: Devices
panels.description: Addresses that opened a connection through the router.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept | count_uniq(source.ip) as devices

panels.title: Destinations
panels.description: Addresses connected to through the router.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept | count_uniq(destination.ip) as destinations

panels.title: DNS around Pi-hole
panels.description: DNS from the LAN or the IoT VLAN straight to a server on the internet (DnsToOutsideServer). The lab VLAN is left out: Pi-hole's own upstream leaves from there.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept destination.port:in(53, 853) observer.egress.interface.name:in(wgc1, ppp0) source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") -source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.111.0/24") | count() as connections

panels.title: Connections by way out
panels.description: Accepted connections by the interface they left on.

targets.expr: {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept | stats by (observer.egress.interface.name) count() as connections

panels.title: Straight out (not through the VPN)
panels.description: Devices whose connections left without the VPN (ppp0), the busiest first.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept observer.egress.interface.name:=ppp0 | stats by (source.ip) count() as connections, count_uniq(destination.ip) as destinations, count_uniq(destination.port) as ports | sort by (connections desc) | limit 50

panels.title: DNS to servers on the internet
panels.description: Every connection to port 53 or 853 out through the VPN or straight out. Expected: the lab VLAN's Pi-hole nodes (unbound to Mullvad, 10.64.0.1) and the router's own fallback (its tunnel address, 10.67.x).

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept destination.port:in(53, 853) observer.egress.interface.name:in(wgc1, ppp0) | stats by (source.ip, destination.ip, destination.port, observer.egress.interface.name) count() as connections | sort by (connections desc) | limit 50

panels.title: Between networks
panels.description: Connections from one of the router's networks to another, by where they went.

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=accept observer.egress.interface.name:~"^br" | stats by (source.ip, destination.ip, network.transport, destination.port) count() as connections | sort by (connections desc) | limit 50

panels.title: Known-bad lookups
panels.description: DNS lookups of a domain on the lists (DnsLookupOfKnownBadDomain). abuse.ch's ThreatFox (the last 48 hours) and URLhaus (hosts serving malware now), and Spamhaus's DROP for addresses (networks run by criminals); subdomains of a listed domain and addresses in a listed network match too; matched as the lines came in (vector-aggregator, refreshed every 6 hours).

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=dns-query threat.enrichments.matched.field:"dns.question.name" | count() as lookups

panels.title: Known-bad answers
panels.description: Answers resolving an unlisted name to a listed address (DnsAnswerWithKnownBadIp). abuse.ch's ThreatFox (the last 48 hours) and URLhaus (hosts serving malware now), and Spamhaus's DROP for addresses (networks run by criminals); subdomains of a listed domain and addresses in a listed network match too; matched as the lines came in (vector-aggregator, refreshed every 6 hours).

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=dns-reply threat.enrichments.matched.field:"dns.resolved_ip" -threat.enrichments.matched.field:"dns.question.name" | count() as answers

panels.title: Known-bad addresses seen
panels.description: Lines with a listed address as source or destination, without the internet's dropped packets (TrafficWithKnownBadIp). abuse.ch's ThreatFox (the last 48 hours) and URLhaus (hosts serving malware now), and Spamhaus's DROP for addresses (networks run by criminals); subdomains of a listed domain and addresses in a listed network match too; matched as the lines came in (vector-aggregator, refreshed every 6 hours).

targets.expr: _time:$__range (threat.enrichments.matched.field:"source.ip" or threat.enrichments.matched.field:"destination.ip") -(event.action:=drop -source.ip:ipv4_range("192.168.0.0/16") -source.ip:ipv4_range("10.0.0.0/8") -source.ip:ipv4_range("172.16.0.0/12")) | count() as lines

panels.title: Dropped from known-bad
panels.description: Packets from listed addresses on the internet the firewall dropped: expected, no alert. abuse.ch's ThreatFox (the last 48 hours) and URLhaus (hosts serving malware now), and Spamhaus's DROP for addresses (networks run by criminals); subdomains of a listed domain and addresses in a listed network match too; matched as the lines came in (vector-aggregator, refreshed every 6 hours).

targets.expr: _time:$__range {event.dataset="syslog.log"} host.ip:="192.168.111.1" event.action:=drop threat.enrichments.matched.field:"source.ip" | count() as packets

panels.title: Matches
panels.description: Every line that matched, by what matched and where: the indicator's page on abuse.ch or Spamhaus in Reference. abuse.ch's ThreatFox (the last 48 hours) and URLhaus (hosts serving malware now), and Spamhaus's DROP for addresses (networks run by criminals); subdomains of a listed domain and addresses in a listed network match too; matched as the lines came in (vector-aggregator, refreshed every 6 hours).

targets.expr: _time:$__range threat.enrichments.matched.atomic:* | replace_regexp (`^\["|"\]$`, "") at threat.enrichments.matched.atomic | replace (`","`, ", ") at threat.enrichments.matched.atomic | replace_regexp (`^\["|"\]$`, "") at threat.enrichments.matched.field | replace (`","`, ", ") at threat.enrichments.matched.field | replace_regexp (`^\["|"\]$`, "") at threat.enrichments.indicator.provider | replace (`","`, ", ") at threat.enrichments.indicator.provider | replace_regexp (`^\["|"\]$`, "") at threat.enrichments.indicator.description | replace (`","`, ", ") at threat.enrichments.indicator.description | replace_regexp (`^\["|"\]$`, "") at threat.enrichments.indicator.reference | replace (`","`, ", ") at threat.enrichments.indicator.reference | stats by (event.action, client.ip, source.ip, threat.enrichments.matched.atomic, threat.enrichments.matched.field, threat.enrichments.indicator.provider, threat.enrichments.indicator.description, threat.enrichments.indicator.reference) count() as lines, max(_time) as _time | sort by (_time desc) | limit 200
